title: Additive representations by powerful integers
summary: A saving of order k^(-3/2) for primitive diagonal powerful triples by direct rational compression, a related fixed-offset bound, and pointwise bounds for powerful sums and differences.
abstract:
For all sufficiently large \(k\), the number of primitive
\(k\)-full triples \(a+b=c\le X\) is
\(O_{k,\varepsilon}(X^{2/k-c_0 k^{-3/2}+\varepsilon})\) for an absolute
\(c_0>0\). We reduce each triple with fixed \(c\) to a
congruence between two short rational numbers and count
its solutions with a rectangular determinant.
This also gives a saving of order \(r^{-3/2}\) over
\(1/p+1/q\) for fixed offsets \(p=r+u,\ q=r+v\).
The same manuscript gives bounds for representations by two
positive \(k\)-full integers. Their number at target \(N\) is
\(O_\varepsilon(N^{3/10+\varepsilon})\) for \(k=2\) and
\(O_{k,\varepsilon}(N^{1/(k+1)+\varepsilon})\) for \(k\ge3\).
The graph bounds used for these estimates also apply to
large coprime differences.

verification.scope: Written proofs, scoped primary-source inspection, exact arithmetic checks, rational certificate replay and visual review of the seventeen-page PDF.
verification.limits: Independent PDF-only review, specialist review, formal verification and exhaustive priority search remain unperformed.
